order.text: Mechanical parts last; before that, low parts before tall parts and robust parts before heat-sensitive parts.

capacitor_by_value.text: Without a type or package in the BOM, a capacitor below the first limit counts as ceramic, from the second limit as electrolytic, in between as unclear.

label: wire jumper
wire jumpers
kinds.action: Solder the {what} flat on the board.

hints.text: Lowest parts first, so the board lies flat while you solder (rule of thumb).

label: resistor
resistors
kinds.action: Solder the {what} flat on the board.

hints.text: Low parts early, so the board lies flat while you solder (rule of thumb).
Point the colour bands the same way; that makes checking the values easier (rule of thumb).

label: diode
diodes
kinds.action: Solder the {what}; the band marks the cathode.

hints.text: Polarised: the band marks the cathode (onsemi 1N4001). Match it to the cathode mark on the board.
evidence: Polarity: Cathode Indicated by Polarity Band

hints.text: Keep each joint short and let the part cool before the next joint (rule of thumb).
Keep each joint short (rule of thumb); the soldering limits are in the datasheet of the part.

label: transistor
transistors
kinds.action: Solder the {what}; match each pin to its pad.

hints.text: Pinout from the datasheet, do not guess: in the same TO-92 case the onsemi PN2222 is pin 1-2-3 = E-B-C, the onsemi P2N2222A is C-B-E.
evidence: 1. Emitter 2. Base 3. Collector
COLLECTOR 1, BASE 2, EMITTER 3

hints.text: Keep each joint short and let the part cool before the next joint (rule of thumb).

label: IC
ICs
kinds.action: Solder the {what} (or their sockets); pin 1 first.

hints.text: Match pin 1 (notch or dot on the package) to the pin 1 mark on the board; the package drawing in the datasheet shows it (rule of thumb).
Prefer a socket: solder the socket now and insert the IC at the end (rule of thumb).
Keep each joint short and do not solder neighbouring pins one after another (rule of thumb).

label: LED
LEDs
kinds.action: Solder the {what}; the cathode goes to the cathode mark on the board.

hints.text: Polarised: find the cathode in the package drawing of the datasheet; on the Kingbright WP7113GD it is the shorter lead.
evidence: the shorter lead is labelled 'Cathode'

hints.text: The iron must not touch the epoxy lens (Kingbright). Keep each joint short and let the part cool before the next joint (rule of thumb).
evidence: The tip of the soldering iron should never touch the lens epoxy.

hints.text: Bend the leads before mounting, not after soldering (Kingbright).
evidence: Do not perform lead forming once the component has been mounted onto the PCB.

hints.text: Check in the datasheet which pin is the wiper before soldering (rule of thumb).
Many buzzers are polarised (+ mark on the body); check the datasheet (rule of thumb).
Low voltage only: if this relay is meant to switch mains voltage, stop here. Circuit Bench does not cover mains wiring.

label: capacitor of unclear type
capacitors of unclear type
kinds.action: Check whether the {what} are polarised, then solder them.

hints.text: The BOM does not say whether this is a ceramic or an electrolytic capacitor. An aluminium electrolytic has a polarity mark for the negative lead on its sleeve (Rubycon); if you see one, it is polarised. Tell Hermes the type to get the right step.
evidence: (4)Polarity (Negative Polarity)

label: electrolytic capacitor
electrolytic capacitors
kinds.action: Solder the {what}; the stripe on the sleeve marks minus.

hints.text: Polarised: reverse voltage can open the pressure relief vent (Nichicon). The stripe on the sleeve marks the negative lead (Rubycon). Confirm the polarity before soldering.
evidence: Aluminum electrolytic capacitors are polarized.
The pressure relief vent may operate due to generation of gas caused by reverse voltage
(4)Polarity (Negative Polarity)

hints.text: The iron must not touch the capacitor body (Nichicon).
evidence: solder iron does not touch any portion of capacitor body

hints.text: Do not tilt, lay down or twist the body once it is soldered (Nichicon).
evidence: Do not tilt lay down or twist the capacitor body

hints.text: Unknown part type: check height, polarity and pinout in its datasheet before soldering. If it is a connector or another mechanical part, solder it with the connectors.
Mechanical parts last (rule of thumb).
Solder one pin, check that the header sits straight and flat, then solder the rest (rule of thumb).
Press the switch flat onto the board while you solder the first pin (rule of thumb).
Solder one pin, check the alignment, then solder the rest (rule of thumb).
Point the wire openings towards the board edge before soldering (rule of thumb).

label: module
modules
kinds.action: Fit the {what} last, preferably into female headers.

hints.text: Plug the module into female headers instead of soldering it in, so you can remove it later (rule of thumb).
Before you plug it in: look for solder bridges and check with a multimeter that the supply rails are not shorted to GND (rule of thumb).

label: battery
batteries
kinds.action: Fit the {what} last, in a holder.

hints.text: Do not solder directly onto a battery: it can leak, short internally, catch fire or explode (Panasonic). Use a holder and insert the cell last.
evidence: Direct soldering onto batteries may damage the resin in crimping, separator and other parts, causing electrolyte leak, internal short circuit, fire and explosion.
Do not solder directly onto the battery.

hints.text: Insert the cell with the correct polarity (Panasonic).
evidence: Insert the batteries in correct polarity position.

kind_by_value.text: {refs}: type guessed from the value only. If a part has a minus stripe on its sleeve, it is an electrolytic and polarised (Rubycon).
evidence: (4)Polarity (Negative Polarity)

led_strip_data.text: {refs}: solder the wires at the input end of the strip; the arrows on the strip point away from DIN, in the direction of the data (rule of thumb).

led_strip_supply.text: {refs}: a long strip draws its current through the supply wires; size them for the current from bench_calc led_strip (rule of thumb).

module_mount_unknown.text: {refs}: the module catalog does not say whether it comes with pin headers or only solder pads; check the module's datasheet before you plan female headers (rule of thumb).

text_rules.text: {refs}: laser. Never look into the beam and never aim it at anyone (FDA). Keep the laser unplugged while you solder (rule of thumb).
evidence: you should never look directly into any laser beam
Never aim or shine a laser pointer at anyone.

text_rules.text: {refs}: lithium cell. Do not solder directly onto the cell (Panasonic); use a holder or connector, check the polarity and connect the cell last.
evidence: Do not solder directly onto the battery.
Insert the batteries in correct polarity position.

text_rules.text: {refs}: mains voltage mentioned. Circuit Bench covers low-voltage circuits only; do not use this plan for mains wiring.

actions.led_strip: Wire the {what} at its input end: {count} wires ({wires}).
actions.module_neutral: Fit the {what} last, mounted as the board is built (pin headers or solder pads).
